title: New Fertility Research Offers Hope for Aging Eggs
subtitle: Scientists develop a way to stabilize chromosomes, potentially helping those who choose to have children later in life.

summary.en: Many people are now waiting longer to have children, but this often leads to biological challenges. As eggs age, they struggle to keep their chromosomes organized, which can cause infertility and miscarriage. Researchers at the Max Planck Institute have created a new protein system to fix this issue in mouse eggs. This discovery could eventually lead to better outcomes for IVF treatments in humans. Experts believe this work is a significant step forward for reproductive science.
summary.zh: 許多人現在選擇較晚生育，但這往往會帶來生物學上的挑戰。隨著卵子老化，它們難以維持染色體的組織結構，這可能導致不孕與流產。馬克斯普朗克研究所的研究人員創造了一種新的蛋白質系統，以修復小鼠卵子中的此類問題。這項發現最終可能改善人類試管嬰兒療程的結果。專家認為，這項研究是生殖科學向前邁出的重要一步。

paragraphs.en: Across the globe, more people are choosing to start families later in life for many social and economic reasons. However, this trend brings a difficult biological challenge: as people age, their eggs become less likely to produce a healthy pregnancy. A new study published in the journal Science offers a potential solution to this problem, building on previous research about how egg cells function over time.
paragraphs.zh: 在全球各地，由於許多社會與經濟因素，越來越多人選擇晚婚晚育。然而，這種趨勢帶來了一項艱鉅的生物學挑戰：隨著年齡增長，卵子產生健康懷孕的可能性會降低。近期發表在《科學》期刊上的一項研究，基於先前關於卵細胞隨時間運作方式的研究，為此問題提供了一種潛在的解決方案。

paragraphs.en: According to STAT News, the primary cause of age-related fertility issues is a condition called aneuploidy. This happens when chromosomes—the structures that carry our genetic information—fail to separate correctly during cell division. This problem becomes much more common after the age of 40. Data shows that between 50% and 80% of embryos from women in their 40s have these chromosomal errors. These mistakes are the main reason for failed in-vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles and miscarriages.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《STAT新聞》報導，與年齡相關的生育問題主要起因於一種稱為「非整倍體」的狀況。當染色體（即攜帶遺傳資訊的結構）在細胞分裂過程中無法正確分離時，就會發生這種情況。此問題在四十歲後變得非常普遍。數據顯示，四十多歲女性的胚胎中，有百分之五十到八十存在這些染色體錯誤。這些錯誤是導致試管嬰兒療程失敗與流產的主要原因。

paragraphs.en: To understand why this happens, it is helpful to look at how egg cells work. When a cell prepares to divide, it uses a protein complex called cohesin. Cohesin acts like a "molecular glue" that holds chromosomes together until they are ready to separate. In most cells, this process happens quickly. However, in eggs, this glue must hold the chromosomes together for decades. Female babies are born with all the egg cells they will ever have, and these cells must keep their cohesin in place until fertilization occurs. Over many years, this glue naturally wears out, which leads to the errors seen in older eggs.
paragraphs.zh: 要理解為何會發生這種情況，觀察卵細胞的運作方式很有幫助。當細胞準備分裂時，會使用一種稱為「黏連蛋白」的蛋白質複合物。黏連蛋白就像一種「分子膠水」，將染色體固定在一起，直到它們準備好分離為止。在大多數細胞中，這個過程發生得很快。然而在卵子中，這種膠水必須將染色體固定數十年之久。女性嬰兒出生時就擁有了她一生中所有的卵細胞，而這些細胞必須在受精發生前保持黏連蛋白的穩定。經過多年後，這種膠水會自然耗損，進而導致高齡卵子中出現上述錯誤。

paragraphs.en: In a significant breakthrough, researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences in Germany have engineered a new protein system to solve this. Led by Melina Schuh, the team spent eight years testing different designs to see if they could replace or support the aging glue. They eventually created a system called "TALhesins." These proteins are designed to attach to the chromosomes and keep them stable, even when the natural cohesin has deteriorated. In their latest experiments, the team successfully used this system to restore normal chromosome connections in aging mouse eggs.
paragraphs.zh: 在一項重大突破中，德國馬克斯普朗克多學科科學研究所（Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences）的研究人員設計出一種新的蛋白質系統來解決此問題。在梅琳娜·舒（Melina Schuh）的帶領下，該團隊花了八年時間測試不同的設計，試圖找出能否取代或輔助老化的膠水。他們最終創造出一種稱為「TALhesins」的系統。這些蛋白質旨在附著於染色體上並保持其穩定，即使在天然黏連蛋白已經退化的情況下亦然。在最新的實驗中，該團隊成功利用此系統恢復了老化小鼠卵子中正常的染色體連結。

paragraphs.en: While the research is still in the early stages, it has gained attention from experts in the field. Rajiv McCoy, a biologist at Johns Hopkins University who was not part of the study, described the results as a successful "proof of concept." This means the team has shown that their idea works in a laboratory setting. McCoy noted that because aneuploidy is the leading cause of pregnancy loss, any technology that can address this issue could have a massive impact on the IVF industry and society. He emphasized that the "stakes are very high" for families hoping to have children.
paragraphs.zh: 雖然這項研究仍處於早期階段，但已引起該領域專家的關注。未參與此研究的約翰霍普金斯大學（Johns Hopkins University）生物學家拉吉夫·麥考伊（Rajiv McCoy）將此結果描述為成功的「概念驗證」。這意味著該團隊已證明其構想在實驗室環境中是可行的。麥考伊指出，由於非整倍體是導致懷孕失敗的主因，任何能解決此問題的技術都可能對試管嬰兒產業與社會產生巨大影響。他強調，對於渴望擁有孩子的家庭來說，這項研究的「利害關係非常重大」。

paragraphs.en: Despite the excitement, the path to using this in humans is long. The researchers must ensure that the process is safe and effective for human eggs before it can ever be used in a medical clinic. For now, the study provides a new way to look at the biology of aging. By understanding how to stabilize chromosomes, scientists hope to one day expand the biological window for reproduction, giving more people the chance to have healthy pregnancies later in life.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管令人振奮，但將此技術應用於人類的道路依然漫長。研究人員必須確保該過程對人類卵子是安全且有效的，才能在醫療診所中使用。目前，這項研究提供了一種看待老化生物學的新視角。透過理解如何穩定染色體，科學家希望有朝一日能延長生育的生物學窗口，讓更多人在較晚的年紀也有機會獲得健康的懷孕。

paragraphs.en: This study is an important update to the ongoing conversation about fertility. As the scientific community continues to explore these new methods, the focus will remain on how to turn these laboratory successes into real-world treatments. For many, this research offers a glimmer of hope that the biological limits of aging might one day be managed with more success than ever before.
paragraphs.zh: 這項研究是關於生育議題持續對話中的重要進展。隨著科學界持續探索這些新方法，焦點將放在如何將這些實驗室的成功轉化為現實世界的治療手段。對許多人而言，這項研究提供了一線希望，即老化的生物學限制有朝一日或許能比以往更成功地被克服。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To become damaged or less effective through long-term use or age.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 磨損、耗損、因長期使用而失效。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於物品損壞，這裡指生物機制隨時間老化失效。文中：Over many years, this glue naturally wears out, which leads to the errors seen in older eggs.

keyTerms.definitionEn: The risks involved in a situation, or what is at risk of being lost or gained.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（下注），這裡指重要性與風險極高。文中：He emphasized that the "stakes are very high" for families hoping to have children.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A limited period of time during which something can happen.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（窗戶），這裡指時間上的限制。文中：scientists hope to one day expand the biological window for reproduction, giving more people the chance to have healthy pregnancies later in life.

previousArticles.summaryEn: Many people are choosing to have children later in life, but this often leads to biological difficulties. A new study from the Max Planck Institute has found a way to support chromosomes in aging eggs. By using a new protein system, scientists successfully stabilized these structures in mouse eggs. This discovery could eventually help improve the success rates of in-vitro fertilization. Experts believe this work is a significant step forward in understanding and preventing pregnancy loss.

quiz.question: What is the primary biological reason that aging egg cells struggle to produce healthy pregnancies?

options.A: The eggs are produced too late in a woman's life.
options.B: Chromosomes fail to separate correctly during cell division.
options.C: The protein complex cohesin is produced in excess amounts.
options.D: The body stops producing necessary proteins after age 40.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第二段明確指出，與年齡相關的生育問題主因是「非整倍體」（aneuploidy），即染色體在細胞分裂過程中無法正確分離。選項 A 錯誤，因為女性出生時就已擁有所有卵子，並非晚年才產生。選項 C 錯誤，文中提到的是 cohesin 會隨時間「磨損」（wears out），而非過量產生。選項 D 錯誤，文中並未提到身體停止製造蛋白質，而是指現有的蛋白質結構失效。

quiz.question: Based on the article, why is it significantly more difficult for human eggs to maintain chromosome stability compared to other cells in the body?

options.A: Human eggs are larger than other cells and require more energy.
options.B: Other cells divide more frequently, preventing the accumulation of errors.
options.C: Egg cells must keep their cohesin glue functional for decades.
options.D: The protein cohesin is only present in human reproductive cells.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第三段，其他細胞的染色體分離過程發生得很快，但卵子細胞內的 cohesin 必須維持數十年，因為女性出生時就帶有所有卵子，這導致蛋白質隨時間老化。選項 A 文中未提及。選項 B 雖然正確描述了其他細胞的特徵，但並非解釋「為什麼卵子更難維持穩定」的核心原因。選項 D 錯誤，文中提到 cohesin 存在於「大多數細胞」（in most cells）中。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the phrase 'proof of concept' imply about the research?

options.A: The researchers have successfully demonstrated that their theory works in a lab.
options.B: The treatment has been proven safe for human clinical use.
options.C: The researchers have obtained a patent for their new protein system.
options.D: The study has been fully rejected by the scientific community.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中提到 Rajiv McCoy 將此研究描述為「proof of concept」，並緊接著解釋這意味著團隊已在實驗室環境中證明其想法可行。選項 B 錯誤，第六段明確指出該技術距離人類應用還有很長的路要走，尚未證明安全性。選項 C 文中未提及專利。選項 D 錯誤，文中提到該研究獲得了領域內專家的關注與重視，並非被拒絕。

quiz.question: What is the main message of the article?

options.A: Aneuploidy is an unavoidable part of human aging that cannot be treated.
options.B: Scientists have successfully developed a permanent cure for infertility in women.
options.C: New research offers a potential way to address age-related fertility issues by stabilizing chromosomes.
options.D: The IVF industry is currently failing because it does not use advanced technology.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。整篇文章圍繞著由 Max Planck Institute 開發的「TALhesins」系統，旨在解決因染色體不穩定導致的生育問題，雖處於早期階段，但為未來提供了希望。選項 A 錯誤，文章正是為了探討如何克服此問題。選項 B 過於誇大，文中強調這僅是實驗室階段，尚未應用於人類。選項 D 錯誤，文章並未批評 IVF 產業本身，而是探討如何透過新技術改善其成功率。
